title: Perf run 20261016-1616
heading: The start page shows its board about 150 ms sooner on a phone
meta:
On a phone, the start page now places its picture of the board from a small script in the page, before the app's own script has loaded. On b0efe05, the branch's last code commit, against the base f294faf, cold load, 8 pairs: a phone shows the board after 576 ms instead of 733 ms (−21%, every pair faster, not called), and its first paint is called better (−39%). Becoming usable moved by ×1.01 at the median pair, the small cost you accepted.

Desktops and tablets keep the page as it was. With the picture placed early there too, a desktop's board showed about 60 ms sooner, but its first click was answered about 2.5 ms later (×1.275 at the median pair, not called). You said yes for phones, so that trade is parked for you to decide later (SP5).

The run also queued the computer's searches when its worker fails, removed a wrapper that r3f 9.8 made dead, fixed an error screen that the early picture could hide, and taught the bench a returning phone and the machine's state at each run. A year's cache for built files waits on you.

items.title: Three headline rows lean slower (none called)
items.body:
The skill asks me to list any headline row worse in every pair, or more than 3% worse at the median pair, even when the comparison does not call it.

  • Desktop, the start page shows the board (b0efe05 against f294faf, cold load, 8 pairs, ab-20261016-1616-sp4-phone.md): median pair ×1.034, 5 of 8 slower (1.02 1.04 0.68 1.05 1.14 1.42 0.81 0.92). The desktop now runs the base's code plus a 2.4 KB script that stops at once, and the pairs span 0.68–1.42.
  • Playing the computer, first board picture (6dc0af5 against f294faf, 8 pairs, ab-20261016-1616-final.md): 1.21 → 1.27 s, median pair ×1.049, 5 of 8 slower (1.09 0.92 1.04 1.09 1.06 1.07 0.98 0.97).
  • The player's move appears (same comparison): 268 → 280 ms, median pair ×1.045, 5 of 8 slower (1.22 1.08 1.06 1.03 0.98 0.94 0.94 1.16).

No code from this run runs on the last two. The head side also holds main's #159 and #160, which restyle the move record that a move updates. The desktop's first click (×1.275) and usable (×1.04) on the final comparison came from the early picture, which b0efe05 takes off the desktop.

items.title: 0930:17: keep built files in the browser's cache for a year
items.body:
With /assets/* cached for a year, a returning phone's start page is usable after 402 ms instead of 557 ms (every pair 0.66–0.74, called better). It needs 2 requests instead of 18.5. First visits do not change.

The cost: a click made the instant the button works is answered after 624 ms instead of 38.8 ms (every pair 14–22 times slower, called worse). The returning board on screen is +18% (not called), and first paint is +14%. With the scene's code already cached, the browser runs it and builds the preview exactly when that click lands.

One caveat came up in review. The base side of that comparison was served with the preview server's default headers, not the host's. The committed bench without the cache rule reads 568–571 ms and 15 requests, so the gain is about as large. It should still be measured again on the committed bench.

charts.caption: Returning phone, with the year's cache against without it, 6 pairs (ab-20261016-1616-cache.md).

items.recommend: Not yet. The next run tries to hold the preview's build until the page's first input or an idle moment on a returning visit (RC1). That would keep the faster page without the slow first click. The patch is kept in bench/loop/patches/assets-cache-0930-17.patch.

scoreboard.intro:
The headline rows are the moments a player waits for, listed in bench/primary.mjs. On 6dc0af5 against f294faf, 8 pairs: ×1.055 over the 15 rows, none called better or worse. b0efe05 then took the early picture off desktops and tablets; it changes only the start page, which was measured again on it (cold load, 8 pairs): the phone's board −21%, every pair faster; the phone's first paint called better on a first visit (−39%) and a returning one (−30%); the desktop rows back at the base's, none called. Geometries grown over 16 moves stay at 10, and textures at 0 (6dc0af5).

At the start of the run, f294faf against the last run's base was ×0.996, none called.

This run did not measure against the first recorded run (92ce041). The last measurement stands: e02a235 was 2.48 times as fast over the 11 rows both can measure, against a target of 1.2.

changed.intro: One change is for speed (SP4, on phones). The others fix behaviour, remove dead code, or let the bench see more.

items.title: On a phone, the start page's picture is placed before the app's script runs (SP4, f20a29f, b0efe05)
items.body: Before, React placed the picture of the board after the app's script had loaded and run. Now, in a phone's window, a 2.4 KB script inside the built page places the same picture as the page is parsed. When React renders the start page, it takes that very element in as its own, so the picture is fetched and decoded once. On b0efe05: a phone shows the board after 576 ms instead of 733 ms, every pair faster. Tests hold the two markups equal at three phone sizes, check that a tablet or desktop window gets none, run the built script, and cap its size at 3,200 bytes.

items.title: An error on the start page is no longer hidden under the picture (6dc0af5)
items.body: Review found that if the start page failed to render, the error screen sat under SP4's opaque picture: no words, and a link that worked but could not be seen. The error screen now removes the early picture. A test fails without the fix.

items.title: The computer's searches on the page run one at a time (RV17, 6464f00)
items.body: When the computer's worker fails to load, its search runs on the page. A review with three such searches took the page in turns with no frame between them. They now queue, each after a short wait. A test needs at least 25 ms between three answers and fails without the queue. Only the fallback path changes.

items.title: The bench measures a returning phone (49d692e)
items.body: The cold-load section now also loads the start page a second time on the same phone, with its cache, and counts the requests to the server. Its headline row is "Start page usable, phone, returning": about 570 ms with 15 requests, against about 680 ms on a first visit. The preview server now sends the host's headers from public/_headers, so the cache behaves as a player's would.

items.title: Each comparison records the machine's state (AA1, f8cc5dc, 0b4c53e)
items.body: Every A/B report now has a table of the machine as each run began: the gap since the last run, the load, CPU and disk waiting, free memory, and leftover processes. The final comparison shows no leftover processes, while the load stayed at 3–5 after each run. So the order effect between the two runs of a pair is not caused by leftovers. The next run tries waiting for the CPU to settle.

items.title: The A/B report applies the speed rule itself (4032946)
items.body: The report now lists each headline row that is worse in every pair or more than 3% worse at its median pair. Review found two counts done by hand wrong this run. The same commit stops the bench from crashing on machines without /proc, such as a Mac.

items.title: Checks that could not fail now can (dc452c5, e7fca16)
items.body: The reconnect's timer and the CSS fallbacks each gained a test that fails when the code it guards is removed. The built page's early script now runs in a test. The docs test names the phrase it reads.

removed.intro:
pointerEvents.ts and its test are gone (−44 lines), with the two props that used it (aba8f50). It worked round an r3f race that the installed r3f 9.8.1 no longer has: its root mounts inside the canvas's layout effect. An e2e test now leaves the start page and the tutorial the moment their canvases appear.

Against main, outside bench/loop/, the app's code grows by 146 lines net (+193, −47): SP4's early picture and its build step, the preview server's headers (used only by vite preview), the search queue and the error-screen fix. Tests grow by 227 net, the bench by 143, and ARCHITECTURE.md by 6.

rejected.intro: 0930:17 is not rejected. It waits on you, under Needs from me. The early picture on desktops and tablets is parked, not rejected (SP5, bench/loop/patches/early-picture-desktop-SP5.patch): it showed a desktop's board about 60 ms sooner but answered its first click about 2.5 ms later, a trade you were not asked about.

items.title: SP4 as first written: swap the picture when React's copy has decoded
items.body: Against the form that landed, which takes the early element in at once, it was no better on any row. The landed form leaned better on the phone (usable −2.0%, board −5.4%, not called) and is about 15 lines shorter (ab-20261016-1616-sp4-adopt-vs-patch.md).

choices.intro:
• I limited SP4 to the phone layout. Your yes named phones; on a desktop it also slowed the first click, a trade you were not asked about. Tablets go with desktops: they are not phones, and the bench does not measure them.
  • I landed the returning-phone measurement without the year's cache that it was built for, because the cache trades one moment against another.
  • I kept the search queue without a timing row: the bench never meets a failed worker.
  • I kept the leave-at-once e2e test although it cannot fail on today's r3f. It guards against a future change in r3f and costs about 1 s.
  • I fixed the error screen under the picture in this run rather than logging it: SP4 caused it, and the fix is 4 lines.
  • Commit messages are not rewritten. The messages of f20a29f ("4 of 8 pairs", "+4.0%") and 49d692e ("557 ms, 18.5 requests") carry figures that review found wrong. The run record and the PR give the corrected ones.

notConfirmed.intro:
• SP4 in a real browser on the built page was checked by hand once (one image, one picture request). No e2e test runs against the build (EB1).
  • The /proc guard has not run on a Mac.
  • What causes the order effect between the runs of a pair (AA1). Leftover processes are ruled out.
